clue.text: Frank talks with Arthur — possibly aired for your benefit?

parts.note: King Arthur's knights met at the Round Table, so the legendary king calls up that piece of furniture
frank talks are open, candid exchanges of views, which is what a discussion is

explanation.surface: A candid chat with someone called Arthur, perhaps broadcast for the listener's good.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue's first half reads as a name and a chat, but Arthur points to his knights' famous table, and the frank talks are the second word.
explanation.definitionFit: A panel debate of this kind is a staple of public-affairs radio and television, broadcast to inform the audience.

clue.text: If it does, might your pet come down with it in the fall?

definitions.text: If it does, might your pet come down with it in the fall?

parts.words: If it does, might your pet come down with it in the fall?
parts.note: a whimsical picture of household pets literally dropping out of the sky with a downpour, the fall being the falling of the rain

explanation.walkthrough: The joke takes the idiom for a very heavy downpour at face value: if the weather really did this, a cat or dog could arrive with the fall of water.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes extremely heavy rainfall; the clue imagines the animals in the phrase actually descending with it.

clue.text: The first thing one does in a standard display?

definitions.text: The first thing one does in a standard display?

parts.words: The first thing one does in a standard display?
parts.note: a standard is a flag, and before a flag can be shown off it must be opened out from its furled state

explanation.walkthrough: 'Standard' looks like an adjective meaning ordinary; here it is a noun, a banner or flag, and displaying one starts by spreading it out.
explanation.definitionFit: To open out a rolled flag or sail is the verb's usual sense, the first step in flying a banner.

clue.text: The beginning of scale drawings from him?

definitions.text: The beginning of scale drawings from him?

parts.words: The beginning of scale drawings from him?
parts.note: the opening two notes of the sol-fa scale, read as the surname of an illustrator whose drawings are famous

explanation.walkthrough: 'Scale' suggests scale drawings, but it is the musical scale, whose first two notes are do and re, together DORE. Gustave Doré was a French illustrator famous for his engravings of the Bible and Dante.
explanation.definitionFit: Doré was a nineteenth-century illustrator, so drawings come from him.

clue.text: Overturn a throne — but not this one.

indicators.note: to overturn something is to upset it, so the letters of the words a throne are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A revolutionary call to topple a king's seat, but some other seat than this one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Overturn a throne' reads as a coup, but it is the instruction to rearrange the seven letters of A THRONE.
explanation.definitionFit: Another means a different one, i.e. one that is not this particular one.

clue.text: Rulings that many suits have to some extent.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: lines ruled on paper, a lining in the old sense of marking with lines

definitions.text: that many suits have to some extent
definitions.meaning: second meaning: the inner layers of cloth sewn into jackets and trousers, often only partly

explanation.walkthrough: 'Rulings' wants to mean judgments by a court, and 'suits' lawsuits; but the rulings are drawn lines and the suits are clothes, partly backed with inner fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: Tailored garments are commonly fitted with inner fabric layers, and ruled lines on a page can also be called by this word.

clue.text: Fish used as a standard in weight comparison?

definitions.text: Fish used as a standard in weight comparison?

parts.words: Fish used as a standard in weight comparison?
parts.note: a plump river fish whose name gave English the adjective for someone round and well-padded

explanation.walkthrough: To call someone chubby is, by origin, to compare them with this stout freshwater fish, so it serves as the yardstick for plumpness.
explanation.definitionFit: The chub is a thick-bodied European freshwater fish of the carp family, and 'chubby' derives from its name.

clue.text: Locks inside this, for protection.

parts.note: locks are tresses of hair, held inside a fine mesh to keep them tidy and safe

explanation.walkthrough: 'Locks' and 'protection' suggest security hardware; the locks are hair, kept in place by a fine mesh cap.
explanation.definitionFit: A fine mesh worn over the head keeps a person's tresses in place and protects the styling.

clue.text: It might turn out to be genuine, the big order to partners on the floor.

definitions.text: It might turn out to be genuine, the big order to partners on the floor.

parts.words: It might turn out to be genuine, the big order to partners on the floor.
parts.note: the title of a Cole Porter song read as a command to dancers on the dance floor, and its last word is the letters of genuine turned about

explanation.walkthrough: BEGUINE, a slow dance, is GENUINE with its letters rearranged, which is the 'might turn out' joke; the whole song title sounds like an instruction telling couples to start that dance.
explanation.definitionFit: Cole Porter's 1935 standard has a title phrased as an imperative, so it reads as a command to dancing partners.

clue.text: One might make you sleep.

parts.note: a practitioner of the trance-inducing art named after Franz Mesmer could send a subject into sleep

explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads like a description of a dull book or a sleeping pill; it is the person who puts subjects into a trance.
explanation.definitionFit: Franz Mesmer's followers induced hypnotic trances, so such a practitioner can put a subject to sleep.

clue.text: Writing on finer material?

indicators.note: material is the raw stuff to be worked up into something, so the letters of on finer are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: Text inscribed on a better grade of cloth or paper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Finer material' looks like better fabric, but material signals the rearranging. Dante's Inferno, the first part of the Divine Comedy, is the writing meant.
explanation.definitionFit: Dante's poem of Hell is a celebrated piece of literature, so the title stands for a written work.

clue.text: Wanting to work things, by the sound of it.

indicators.note: the phrase tells the solver to go by how the words are pronounced, not how they are spelt

parts.note: to knead is to work dough or clay with the hands, so working things is kneading

explanation.surface: Someone who lacks something and wants a job, judging by appearances.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by the sound of it' says the word for working dough, KNEADING, is pronounced just like the word for lacking something: the K is silent.
explanation.definitionFit: Needing and wanting both describe lacking something required, as in 'found wanting'.

clue.text: Healing priest?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a remedy or restoration to health, used as a noun
second meaning: a French parish priest, a clergyman in charge of a French parish

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a faith healer; the two words are separate senses, one English and one borrowed from French.
explanation.definitionFit: A remedy restores health, and in France the parish clergyman is called the curé.

clue.text: A bad phone connection with me having no French — but it can be scientifically explained.

indicators.note: a bad connection garbles what comes through, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written
non is French for no

explanation.surface: A crackling phone line, a caller with no French, yet some scientist can account for it all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bad' scrambles PHONE, ME and NON (French for no) together; 'connection with' and 'having' only join the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: In science an observable occurrence or fact that can be studied and explained is called by this word.

clue.text: With a couple of seers and an oil can, rub to manipulate.

indicators.note: to manipulate is to handle and rearrange, so the letters of oil can and rub are shuffled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Two prophets, an oil can and a rub-down, as if for a massage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to manipulate' rearranges OIL CAN and RUB. Seers here are eyes, not prophets: the adjective means using both eyes. 'and an' only joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Binocular vision uses two eyes together, so something binocular works with a pair of eyes.

clue.text: With more flavor.

parts.note: a plain comparative description: something with greater savour

explanation.walkthrough: This is a straight definition with no trick; the comparative form matches 'more'.
explanation.definitionFit: The comparative of an adjective meaning full of savour describes food that has stronger, better taste.

clue.text: A mark beginners may start from.

definitions.text: A mark beginners may start from.

parts.words: A mark beginners may start from.
parts.note: the line scored on the ground where unhandicapped runners begin, and the idiom for starting from nothing

explanation.walkthrough: In handicap races the line for runners with no head start is so named, and to start from it means beginning with no advantage, as novices do.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a scored line and the starting line in a race, hence the idiom about starting afresh.

clue.text: Music, wine and entertainment a few years ago, or possibly a take-off connected with it.

definitions.text: possibly a take-off connected with it

parts.note: an air is a tune, a piece of music
port is a fortified wine from Portugal

explanation.surface: An evening of music, wine and a show some years back, or a parody of such things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entertainment a few years ago' is a third hint: Airport was a hit 1970 disaster film. 'take-off' looks like a parody but is an aircraft leaving the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Aircraft take off from runways at an aerodrome, so the place is connected with every departure.

clue.text: One from the USSR, in a logical disguise.

definitions.text: One from the USSR, in a logical disguise.

indicators.note: the letters are disguised by rearrangement, and logically so because the result fits the clue's meaning

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Soviet citizen travelling incognito, cleverly disguised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'logical disguise' rearranges the letters of USSR, IN and A, and the whole clue describes the answer too.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of the former Soviet Union is commonly called by the name of its largest constituent nation.

clue.text: Hardy girl, taking an age to find part of the flooring, perhaps.

parts.note: Tess of the d'Urbervilles is Thomas Hardy's heroine
an era is an age, a long period of history

explanation.surface: A tough young woman spends ages finding a piece of the floor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hardy' looks like an adjective for a tough girl; it is the novelist Thomas Hardy. 'taking' and 'to find' only join the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A tessera is a small tile or cube of stone used in a mosaic floor.

clue.text: When your world is turbulent, it's naturally upset internally.

definitions.text: When your world is turbulent, it's naturally upset internally.

indicators.note: internally says the answer lies within the run of words world is turbulent, across the word breaks

parts.note: the letters sit from the end of world through is to the start of turbulent

explanation.surface: Turmoil in your life naturally leaves you inwardly shaken.
explanation.walkthrough: 'internally' points inside 'worlD IS TURBulent', where the answer sits; and the whole clue also describes it, since turmoil naturally upsets a person.
explanation.definitionFit: To disturb a person is to trouble or agitate them, unsettling their calm.

clue.text: One might leave early, when the medico has nothing on but a sullen expression.

parts.note: medico is slang for doctor, abbreviated Dr
O looks like zero, nothing
a pout is a sulky pushing-out of the lips

explanation.surface: Someone slipping away early as the doctor, wearing nothing, sulks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has nothing on' sounds like a naked doctor, but it only means O is put after DR; 'but' joins the pout.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who quits school or a course before finishing is said to have abandoned it early.

clue.text: The skimper's motto may be unavailing.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: read as two words, ..., the slogan of someone who economises
second meaning: of no use, ineffective

explanation.walkthrough: Split into two words, the answer is a thrifty person's advice; whole, it means pointless.
explanation.definitionFit: Efforts that achieve nothing are futile or of no avail, which is what the adjective means.

clue.text: See 1
Is it logical that some might consider his Wozzeck cold?

definitions.text: Is it logical that some might consider his Wozzeck cold?

parts.words: Is it logical that some might consider his Wozzeck cold?
parts.note: the composer of the opera Wozzeck shares his name with a floating mass of ice, so his music might be thought chilly

explanation.walkthrough: Alban Berg wrote the atonal opera Wozzeck; his surname is also a word for an iceberg, hence the joke that his work might be thought cold.
explanation.definitionFit: The composer's name is the German word for mountain, used in English for a floating ice mass.

clue.text: Catches up by the arm?

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word is written from the bottom upwards

parts.note: to net a fish is to catch it, so catches gives nets

explanation.surface: Someone grabbing another person by the arm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' writes NETS (catches) upwards in this down clue. 'arm' is a weapon, not a limb: the Sten was a British submachine gun of the Second World War. 'by the' only joins.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sten gun was a cheap British submachine gun, a firearm and so an arm.

clue.text: I might get to make an elemental change with the traditionally dumb guy I have an appointment with.

parts.note: the ox is the proverbially dull beast, as in 'dumb ox'
taken as written
a date is an arranged meeting

explanation.surface: A speaker who could make big changes with an appointment alongside a dim-witted fellow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'elemental' points to chemistry: combining with the element oxygen. 'I might get to' and 'with the', 'have an', 'with' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: To oxidate is an old form of oxidise, chemically combining a substance with oxygen.

clue.text: The second person to be the subject of old Broadway musical.

definitions.text: The second person to be the subject of old Broadway musical.

parts.words: The second person to be the subject of old Broadway musical.
parts.note: the archaic second-person pronoun thee, as the one a song is about: the title of a 1931 Gershwin show

explanation.walkthrough: Thee is the old second-person pronoun; a song with 'you' as its subject gives the title, from the patriotic hymn line, of George and Ira Gershwin's 1931 political satire.
explanation.definitionFit: The Gershwins' musical won the first Pulitzer Prize for Drama given to a musical.

clue.text: See 26
Those who serve must also look in a stall for it, perhaps.

parts.note: waiters serve at table; to wait is what those serving do, and Milton's 'they also serve who only stand and wait'
and adds something further, as also does
to see is to look

explanation.surface: Servers too must check a market stall for something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stall' suggests a market booth; it is the verb's noun sense, a delaying tactic. 'must' and 'in' only join.
explanation.definitionFit: A policy of holding back until events unfold is a classic delaying tactic, a way of playing for time.
